answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 1 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the vault schedule in the quill ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the velvet checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 125 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
